label: Early original-phase steps (t<=2) on a specific token set (c, v, i, d, 2; plus q, 3, l, o at t=1)
explanation: Fires almost only in the first three original-phase steps (t=0..2 hold 99.6% of activation mass; t=1 alone holds 57%). It is essentially silent at the delimiter, in the copy phase, and at t>=3. Inside that window, whether it fires depends on which token is input: c, v, i, d and 2 are strongly preferred (rate about 20-24% vs 5% base), with weaker preference for q, 3, l and o at t=1. It also prefers first occurrences of a token. The largest activations come at t=2 on c or v after a 3 2 / c 2 prefix, so the preceding tokens also change the magnitude. Just t<=2 alone gets 0.99 recall but only 0.21 precision. Adding the token set gets dev F1 of about 0.78 with mass recall of 0.83. Whether it fires on a given token at a given position also depends on the earlier tokens in a way this predicate does not capture, so it is only partially explained.
